evals.prompt: Before we touch anything, run a premortem: over the weekend you're going to migrate our production Postgres 12 RDS instance (~400GB) up to Postgres 16, and we can only tolerate about 20 minutes of downtime.
evals.expected_output: Five past-tense failure reasons specific to this migration, each paired with a one-sentence paste-ready preventing instruction, then a full stop — the migration is not started.
expectations: Each failure is phrased as something that already happened (past tense, e.g. 'it failed because...'), not a hypothetical ('it might...').
Each of the five failures is paired with exactly one paste-ready preventing instruction written as a single directive sentence.
The failures are concrete to this Postgres 12->16 / ~400GB / 20-minute-downtime migration (e.g. replication lag, extension incompatibility, downtime overrun), not generic project advice (judgement).
The five reasons span distinct angles (misread intent, unstated assumption, generic drift, genuinely-hard-for-a-model) rather than five restatements of one worry (judgement).
The skill stops after presenting the failures and fixes and does NOT begin the migration — no migration commands, runbook execution, or 'now I'll start by...'.

evals.prompt: /premortem write the launch announcement for our new pricing
evals.expected_output: Five failures for a deliberately under-specified task; at least one names the ambiguity (audience, channel, tone, what actually changed). Fixes given, then it stops.
expectations: Presents exactly five failure reasons, each in past tense with a single paste-ready fix.

At least one failure targets the ambiguity in this request — unclear audience, channel, length, or what the pricing change actually is — under a misread-intent or unstated-assumption angle (judgement).
Failures are specific to writing a pricing-launch announcement, not generic writing advice (judgement).
The skill does NOT draft the announcement — it stops and hands control back to the user.

evals.prompt: Quick one — premortem then just fix the failing CI on main, it's blocking the whole team.
evals.expected_output: Even under time pressure and an explicit 'just fix it', the skill runs the premortem (five failures + fixes) and then stops, waiting for the user rather than starting the fix.
expectations: Presents exactly five past-tense failure reasons, each with one paste-ready preventing instruction.
Failures are concrete to fixing failing CI on main (e.g. fixing a symptom not the cause, breaking other jobs, masking a real test failure), not generic (judgement).
Despite the 'just fix it' pressure, the skill STOPS after the premortem and does not begin diagnosing or fixing CI (no commands run toward the fix).
